misconceptions.claim: Keeping a log automatically establishes chain of custody.
misconceptions.correction: Chain of custody records controlled possession and handling of specific evidence across time.

misconceptions.claim: A forensic image is automatically admissible because it is technically exact.
misconceptions.correction: Technical integrity matters, but authority, scope, documentation, handling, and applicable legal process also affect whether and how evidence may be used.

outcome: Distinguish likely investigation types and identify the first evidence-handling and authority questions.

sections.body: An administrative inquiry may determine policy or employment consequences; a criminal matter may involve law-enforcement authority; civil work may support a dispute; a regulator may assess statutory duties; an industry or standards inquiry may assess conformance. The same log can matter in each setting, but collection scope, notice, privilege, handling, and disclosure rules differ. Classify the purpose before expanding collection or interviewing people.
keyPoints: Do not assume an internal inquiry has criminal-investigation powers.
Investigation type changes stakeholders and handling requirements.
sections.title: Purpose and authority shape the investigation

sections.body: Follow approved incident and evidence procedures: record who collected what, when, where, and how; preserve originals; limit access; and maintain a chain of custody when required. A legal hold may suspend normal deletion. Security teams should avoid unauthorized searches, unsupported accusations, or altering evidence while troubleshooting. Escalate promptly when facts suggest a legal, regulatory, or criminal pathway.
keyPoints: Evidence integrity includes documented handling, not only technical immutability.
A normal retention schedule may change when a hold applies.
sections.title: Preserve evidence without contaminating it

sections.body: Administrative investigations address organizational policy or employment matters; criminal investigations involve statutory offenses and law-enforcement authority; civil matters support claims or disputes; regulatory and industry-standard inquiries assess duties established by regulators or programs. Scope, legal authority, confidentiality, collection method, notice, chain of custody, retention, and communication must match the purpose. Preserve original evidence, document who handled it and when, control access, and escalate through approved counsel or response paths. A technically useful artifact can become unusable when collection is unauthorized, integrity is unclear, or the wrong investigation authority directs the process.
keyPoints: Name the accountable owner, decision criterion, and evidence for each applicable outline topic.
Record the failure consequence and escalation or review trigger rather than assuming a policy label proves operation.
sections.title: Choose investigation authority, process, and evidence handling

sections.body: Administrative investigations establish internal policy or employment facts; civil investigations support claims and disputes; criminal investigations can involve law-enforcement authority and a higher burden of proof; regulatory investigations address a regulator’s statutory remit; industry-standards inquiries examine conformance to a program or standard. The purpose determines who directs the work, collection authority, notice and privacy limits, legal hold/retention, confidentiality and privilege handling, reporting recipient, and evidence standard. Security preserves facts and records provenance; counsel or the authorized authority defines legal process. A technically useful artifact can be unusable or create liability if collected outside authority or without integrity documentation.
keyPoints: Classify the purpose and authority before expanding collection or interviewing people.
Chain of custody documents handling; it does not create authority to collect.
Do not assume an internal inquiry has criminal powers or legal privilege.
sections.title: Choose evidence handling from the investigation purpose

title: Choose an investigation approach that preserves purpose and evidence

workedExamples.reasoning: Preserve logs and relevant devices under approved procedure, involve HR and counsel, determine whether a hold applies, and avoid an improvised search or accusation. The eventual investigation type may evolve as facts and authority develop.
workedExamples.situation: A departing employee appears to have copied sensitive files before notice of resignation.
workedExamples.takeaway: Preservation and authorized escalation come before proving a theory.
workedExamples.title: Suspicious export

workedExamples.reasoning: Open a controlled administrative inquiry, preserve originals and collection metadata, restrict access, and consult counsel. If facts indicate a possible crime or reportable event, counsel and authorized leadership decide whether and how to involve law enforcement or regulators; the security team does not conduct unauthorized searches or make criminal accusations.
workedExamples.situation: A company finds evidence that an administrator copied customer files to personal storage.
workedExamples.takeaway: The same log can be relevant to several proceedings, but collection and disclosure must follow the governing authority.
workedExamples.title: Suspicious administrator activity
